comparator.name: Fiscaal Recht
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines a complete 180-EC pathway with three 60-EC years and no formal route. Year 1 combines foundations across Dutch public, private, criminal, international and European law with introductory tax law, professional ethics and two applied projects. Year 2 develops individual and director-major-shareholder taxation alongside property, obligations, administrative and criminal law and concludes with a tax-procedure project. Year 3 adds entrepreneurial, corporate, European and international taxation, European and company law, legal philosophy, civil procedure, fundamental rights, an economic integration course and a 6-EC bachelor thesis. The weekly Amsterdam Law Firm is integrated skills teaching and carries no separately published EC, so it is not counted as a separate credited component. The listed credited components total exactly 180 EC.
components: Compulsory independent bachelor thesis using legal research and writing skills developed across the programme.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme's tax-law identity, legal analysis, national and international tax-system foundations and independent legal research. Two further generator-backed directions remain. Business taxation and the legal treatment of business income support a commercial-law, finance and business-regulation route. Fair tax policy, the citizen-state relationship, social justice and the design of taxation support a public-law, rights and policy route. Each direction is coherent and feasible at UCR while remaining explicit about the absence of specialist Dutch tax-law teaching. The closest match differs from each related direction by six courses; the two related directions differ by eleven. Both additional candidates are included, reaching the maximum of three alternatives.

alternatives.label: Law, economics & public finance
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines the strongest available UCR law sequence with economics, public finance, accounting, business law, EU institutions and legal communication. The label states those available fields and does not imply that UCR offers a Dutch tax-law degree.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines broad legal foundations and public, private, international, EU, criminal and business law with economics, taxation and public-spending analysis, accounting, finance, empirical research and persuasive legal communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected economics courses with that prerequisite, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. Introductory economics precedes the advanced economics sequence conceptually. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Rhetoric in Action. The final year concentrates advanced private law, EU politics, governance, econometrics, finance and qualitative research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Business, finance & commercial regulation
alternatives.labelReason: The route concentrates the programme's business-taxation, company-law, financial and commercial dimensions in a business-and-economics sequence with supporting international and private law. The label avoids claiming specialist tax-law coverage that UCR cannot provide.
alternatives.concept: A commercially oriented route in which business organisation, accounting, finance, strategy, organisational leadership, market research and economics are combined with private, international and transnational business law and applied communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, constitutional and administrative law, EU law, EU politics, international-relations theory and qualitative social research. It adds digital business strategy, organisational leadership, business and regulation in the age of AI, behavioural economics, market research and applied rhetoric. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising choice shifts from a broad law-and-public-finance comparison to business organisation, commercial decision-making and finance.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Introduction to Economics establish the legal, business and economic strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected courses that formally require it; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation, Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance, Money, Banking & Finance and Market Research. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Persuasive Communication. The final year advances from accounting, macroeconomics and organisational leadership to private law, global governance, finance, econometrics, behavioural economics and independent market research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Public, international & European law
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum centres public authority, constitutional and administrative law, international and EU law, EU politics and public economics, with sociology and research methods supplying the societal context. It is explicitly a related legal direction rather than a tax-law substitute.
alternatives.concept: A public-law and policy route connecting constitutional and administrative authority, international and EU legal orders, human rights and criminal justice with EU politics, international relations, public economics, sociology and empirical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the business-foundations, accounting, international-business, macroeconomics, finance and transnational-business-law courses. It adds sociology, modern and contemporary social theory, political philosophy, peace and conflict, and behavioural economics. Six of the 24 courses differ from the closest match and eleven differ from the business direction. The route is therefore organised around public authority, institutions and society rather than commercial practice.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Introduction to Economics and Introduction to Sociology establish the legal, economic and social foundations in semester 1. Law, Society & Justice precedes every later law course with that formal prerequisite, and Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected advanced economics courses. International law, constitutional law and international-relations theory precede the advanced EU-law, EU-politics and conflict courses conceptually. Introductory rhetoric precedes Rhetoric in Action, and introductory sociology precedes advanced contemporary social theory conceptually. The final semester brings together qualitative methodology, econometrics, behavioural economics and applied public communication. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

blocks: Both introduce the nature, sources and social operation of law; UCR does so through legal, social and normative perspectives.
Both introduce substantive criminal-law reasoning and criminal justice, including accountability and legal safeguards.
Both establish private-law rights and obligations; UCR surveys property, contract, family and related private-law relationships.
Both examine constitutional and administrative institutions, public powers, legal limits and protected rights.
Both introduce international legal sources and institutions; the comparator also integrates introductory EU law.
Both examine legally protected fundamental rights and their normative foundations; UCR focuses on human rights law and philosophy.
Both examine the European Union legal order and its effects on states, citizens and institutions.
Both address legal rules governing business relationships, although UCR concentrates on transnational transactions rather than Dutch company law.
UCR discusses legal and communication ethics in several courses but has no dedicated course on Dutch legal professions and professional codes.
UCR Principles of Private Law includes family relationships but is already aligned to the comparator's broader introductory private-law component; UCR has no separate family-law course.
UCR Principles of Private Law includes property relationships but not a separate Dutch property-law sequence.
UCR Principles of Private Law includes contracts and obligations but is already aligned to introductory private law; UCR has no second dedicated obligations course.
Comparative Constitutional Law includes administrative-law foundations but is already aligned to the first-year combined public-law component; UCR has no separate advanced administrative-law course.
UCR Criminal Law & Criminal Justice is already aligned to the first-year criminal-law foundation; UCR has no second specialist substantive-criminal-law course.
UCR has no dedicated course on Dutch administrative procedure and judicial review.
UCR has no separate course in Dutch criminal procedure.
UCR offers political and human-rights philosophy, but not a separate advanced legal-philosophy component of this programme's scope.
UCR has no dedicated course on Dutch civil procedure.
Both analyse taxation through economic effects, efficiency, equity, public spending and redistribution; UCR approaches the subject as public economics rather than tax law.
UCR Public Economics analyses taxation economically but does not teach the legal system, sources and doctrines of Dutch tax law.
UCR has no dedicated Dutch personal-income and wealth-tax course.
UCR has no course on the Dutch tax treatment of director-major shareholders.
UCR has no dedicated course on entrepreneurial income tax and VAT.
UCR has no dedicated Dutch corporate-income-tax course.
UCR offers EU law and public economics but not European tax law.
UCR offers public international law and global business governance but not substantive international tax law.
Both examine legal or regulatory challenges created by digitalisation; UCR focuses on AI governance, privacy, fairness and business regulation.
Both require students to design and communicate research; UCR teaches qualitative research methods rather than a fiscal-law thesis.
Both develop applied argumentation and advocacy through problem-based work; UCR uses public speaking and debate rather than Dutch tax litigation.
The comparator applies legal research and writing to constitutional reform; no single UCR scheduled course reproduces that integrated legal project.
The comparator integrates private and compensation law in an applied project; UCR has no equivalent Dutch-law project.

notes.text: The Amsterdam programme is a professional academic law degree with a continuous, jurisdiction-specific sequence in Dutch tax law, including personal, entrepreneurial and corporate taxation, tax procedure, European and international tax law, supported by Dutch public, private, criminal and company law and a fiscal legal thesis. UCR can combine public economics and taxation analysis with broad private, public, criminal, international, EU and business law, accounting, finance and research methods. It does not teach the Dutch tax code, fiscal procedure or the named specialist taxes. These pathways therefore compare related legal, economic and institutional fields; none reproduces the external tax-law discipline or its professional qualification path.
